summary: The manual scanner correctly replaces the regex: a 15M-character literal completes in ~50ms where the baseline throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded (reproduced), trailing spaces before each closing quote are removed, and leading/internal spaces, tabs, newlines, doubled single quotes, characters outside literals, empty and space-only literals, double quotes and multi-literal statements all behave as before. Differential testing (~200k exhaustive short strings over {a, space, quote} plus 500k random strings over {a, space, tab, quote, dquote, newline}) found zero divergences from the baseline on quote-balanced inputs; the only divergences are on unbalanced-quote input, which the task explicitly leaves outside the preservation scope and which no call site can produce. Two minor nits: a dead conditional and that undocumented unbalanced-input semantics change.

findings.claim: The condition `if (contentEnd <= literalEnd - 1)` is dead code: contentEnd is initialized to literalEnd - 1 and only ever decreases inside the preceding while loop, so the guard is always true and the closing quote is always appended. It suggests a case that cannot occur and makes the reader hunt for it.
findings.repro: grep -n 'contentEnd' tools/sql-literals.mjs  # contentEnd starts at literalEnd-1 (== j) and only decrements

findings.claim: Behavior on unbalanced-quote input differs from the baseline: the old regex's greedy backtracking could trim trailing spaces inside a fragment that later proves unterminated (for the 6-char string open-quote a space space quote quote, old trims the spaces, new leaves it verbatim), while the new code leaves any unterminated literal verbatim. All ~1400 divergences found by fuzzing are of this kind; no quote-balanced input diverges, no call site (installTrim passes complete statements or individual quoted values) can produce such input, and the task scopes preservation to quote-balanced fragments, so this is informational only.
